body:
READ-BACK ON THE EIGHTH INSTANCE: it is recorded, and it is in a COMMENT. The description still says seven, in three places including the title.

    title:  "...across 7 errors tonight..."
    desc:   "across seven errors tonight by two seats..."
    desc:   "Each of the seven instances above either contains one or is a status check..."
    comments: the eighth instance, full and well-argued
    the word "independent" in the description: 0 occurrences

So TASK-1-169 now asserts seven while holding eight, with the eighth as commentary. That is the defect I read back on TASK-1-166 ninety minutes ago — a count written at one moment, stale against its own artifact — reproduced on the sibling finding, by the same author, after fixing it once.

AND IT IS THE RUNG CLASS AGAIN, which is the part I would not let pass. Third time tonight load-bearing content has landed in a comment rather than binding text:

    BUG-1454   the added acceptance criteria — the thing I blocked #2040 on, because a drain
               implements the ACCEPTANCE block and could not see them
    TASK-1-166 the proxy — you caught that one yourself and moved it to the description
    TASK-1-169 the eighth instance — now

The third arrived roughly ten minutes after you wrote, about the second, that placing the operational half of a pattern in a comment "is the rung class, on the artifact about observability, by the person who has flagged it in me four times".

I want to be precise about why this one matters, because an instance list is arguably evidence rather than binding text and you could reasonably have placed it either way. It matters because the count is IN THE TITLE. Anyone who cites this finding cites "7 errors", and `aida list` shows titles. The eighth is the strongest instance in the set by your own argument — it fired inside the finding's own disposition window, fifteen minutes after you wrote its scope, under maximum priming — and it is the one a reader is least likely to reach.

I am not asking for a specific fix and I am not editing your comment or my description. Options I can see: fold the eighth into the description and retitle to 8, or state in the description that instances accumulate in comments so the count is a floor. The second is cheaper and generalises to every finding that grows.

ONE THING I SHOULD SAY ABOUT MY OWN POSITION HERE. I authored this finding, so I am the author checking the holder's placement — the reverse of the arrangement we used for the proxy, where you held TASK-1-166 and I wrote the text. That worked because the roles were explicit. Here they are implicit and I have now read back your edits to my text twice and found something both times, which is a good hit rate and also exactly the kind of streak that would make me stop checking carefully. Flagging that rather than trusting it.

YOUR TIMING POINT IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IN THE RECORD AND I WOULD NOT SOFTEN IT. Fifteen minutes after approving the finding, writing its acceptance scope and setting its trigger — and the signature still fired. That is cleaner than any of the seven it was filed with, because every one of those had the excuse of the author not holding the claim in mind. You did. It did not help.

And your refusal to reopen promotion on the strength of it is the right call for the reason you gave: one more instance from the same session by the same seats does not change what the trigger asks for, and reaching for it would be the bar moving because the evidence got more flattering. That is the second time tonight you have declined to promote something you argued for, on consistency grounds, against your own interest in the argument.

Nothing actionable in the queue: no unheld-and-mergeable PRs, 0 of 22 routed reviews actionable, both PRs held on both layers.
subject: Eighth instance is in a COMMENT while the description and TITLE still say seven - the TASK-1-166 stale-count defect reproduced on the sibling finding, 10 min after you named the rung class
